summary: The CNN era: deeper, wider and more modular convolutional backbones for vision.

summary: Very large autoregressive LMs, what scale buys you, and how to spend compute.

name: Instruction tuning & alignment
summary: Teaching LMs to follow instructions and human preferences.

name: Parameter-efficient adaptation
summary: Adapt a big frozen model by training only a small number of new parameters.

name: Self-supervised visual learning
summary: Learning visual features without labels: contrastive, mutual-information and masked-prediction methods.

name: Transfer learning & weak supervision

name: Detector-based vision-language pre-training
summary: BERT-style vision-language models built on object-detector region features (2019–2021).

name: End-to-end vision-language pre-training
summary: Vision-language models trained from pixels, without a separate object detector.

name: Contrastive image–text models
summary: Dual encoders that align images and text in one embedding space, enabling zero-shot transfer.

name: Vision-language models on frozen LLMs
summary: Connect a pretrained vision encoder to a frozen large language model through a small trainable bridge.

name: Image captioning
summary: Generating natural-language descriptions of images, and how to evaluate them.

name: Visual question answering & reasoning
summary: Answering questions and reasoning about images in natural language.

name: Object detection & grounding
summary: Finding objects and linking words or phrases to image regions.

name: Datasets & data curation
summary: How training and evaluation data were collected, cleaned and scaled.

name: Training & optimization
summary: Normalisation, initialisation, regularisation, distillation and optimiser fixes that make training work.

name: Distributed training & systems
summary: Parallelism and systems tricks for training models too big for one accelerator.

name: Sparse & mixture-of-experts models
summary: Conditional computation: activate only part of a huge model for each input.

name: Benchmarks, evaluation & robustness
summary: How progress is measured, and how models fail under distribution shift.

name: Discrete & generative image models
summary: Image tokenisers and models that generate images.

name: Unified multitask models
summary: One model, one format, many tasks.

name: LSTM recurrent networks
summary: Gated recurrent networks that keep information over long sequences.

name: Encoder–decoder seq2seq
summary: Encode an input sequence, then decode an output sequence from it.

name: Attention mechanism
summary: Let a decoder look back at the most relevant input positions instead of one fixed vector.

name: WordPiece subword tokens
summary: Split rare words into frequent sub-word pieces so the vocabulary stays small and open.

name: Language-independent subword tokenizer
summary: Train subword models directly on raw text, with no language-specific pre-tokenisation.

name: Dilated convolutional sequence models
summary: Model long sequences with stacked dilated 1-D convolutions that run in linear time.

name: Convolutional seq2seq
summary: A fully convolutional encoder–decoder with gated linear units and per-layer attention.

name: Self-attention
summary: Every token attends to every other token, weighted by learned query–key similarity.

name: Transformer
summary: A sequence model built only from attention and feed-forward layers, with no recurrence.

name: Sinusoidal positional encoding
summary: Add fixed sine/cosine signals so an order-blind Transformer knows token positions.

name: Inducing-point attention (learned latents)
summary: A few learned vectors attend to a large set and summarise it: the idea behind later resamplers and query transformers.

name: Segment-level recurrence & relative positions
summary: Reuse hidden states from earlier segments so attention can reach beyond a fixed context.

name: Gated feed-forward variants (SwiGLU)
summary: Replace the Transformer's ReLU feed-forward with gated linear units for better quality.

name: Latent-array cross-attention (Perceiver)
summary: A small latent array cross-attends to huge inputs, decoupling depth from input size.

name: Rotary position embedding (RoPE)
summary: Encode position by rotating query/key vectors, giving relative-position awareness inside attention.

name: Very deep 3×3 ConvNets
summary: Stack many small 3×3 convolutions; depth alone drives accuracy.

name: Deconvnet feature visualisation
summary: Project activations back to pixel space to see what each CNN layer has learned.

name: Inception module
summary: Parallel convolutions of several sizes in one block, to go deeper and wider at fixed cost.

name: Residual connection
summary: Add a layer's input to its output so very deep networks stay trainable.

name: Wide residual networks
summary: Shallower but wider residual blocks train faster and match very deep ResNets.

name: Cardinality (grouped convolutions)
summary: Split a block into many parallel same-shaped paths; the number of paths is a new scaling axis.

name: Depthwise-separable convolutions
summary: Factor a convolution into per-channel and 1×1 steps to cut computation drastically.

name: Inverted residuals & linear bottlenecks
summary: Expand, filter with depthwise conv, then project back down to thin residual bottlenecks.

name: Neural architecture search
summary: Search for a network's building block automatically instead of designing it by hand.

name: Latency-aware architecture search
summary: Put measured on-device latency into the search objective.

name: Compound model scaling
summary: Scale depth, width and resolution together with one coefficient.

name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
summary: Split an image into patches and feed them to a plain Transformer as tokens.

name: Distillation token (data-efficient ViT)
summary: Train ViTs on ImageNet alone by adding a token that learns from a CNN teacher.

name: Shifted-window hierarchical ViT
summary: Attention inside local windows that shift between layers, with multi-scale feature maps.

name: Scaling laws for vision Transformers
summary: How ViT error falls with model size, data and compute, up to billions of parameters.

name: Convolution–attention hybrids
summary: Stack convolution stages before attention stages to get both inductive bias and capacity.

name: Local video Transformers
summary: Extend windowed attention across space and time for video recognition.

name: Residual post-norm & cosine attention
summary: Stabilise very large vision Transformers and transfer them across resolutions.

name: Word embeddings (skip-gram / CBOW)
summary: Learn dense word vectors by predicting nearby words in huge text corpora.

name: Large-scale RNN language models
summary: Push LSTM language models to billions of words and huge vocabularies.

name: Contextual word vectors
summary: Word vectors that depend on the sentence, taken from a pretrained encoder.

name: Deep bidirectional LM features
summary: Use all internal layers of a pretrained bidirectional LM as features for downstream tasks.

name: Pre-train, then fine-tune
summary: Train one big model on unlabelled data, then fine-tune it briefly for each task.

name: Masked language modelling
summary: Hide some tokens and predict them from context on both sides.

name: Unified LM via attention masks
summary: One Transformer does bidirectional, left-to-right and seq2seq modelling by switching attention masks.

name: Permutation language modelling
summary: Autoregressive training over all factorisation orders, capturing bidirectional context without masks.

name: Robustly optimised BERT recipe
summary: Train BERT longer, on more data, with bigger batches and dynamic masking.

name: Cross-layer parameter sharing
summary: Share weights across layers and factorise embeddings to shrink BERT.

name: Text-to-text framing
summary: Cast every task as text in, text out: one model, one loss.

name: Span-corruption denoising
summary: Replace random spans with sentinels and train the decoder to fill them in.

name: Denoising seq2seq pre-training
summary: Corrupt text in many ways and train an encoder–decoder to reconstruct it.

name: Mixture-of-denoisers objective
summary: Train on a mix of short-span, long-span and prefix denoising tasks.

name: Autoregressive language modelling
summary: Predict the next token, so the model can generate text left to right.

name: In-context / few-shot learning
summary: A large model solves a new task from a few examples in its prompt, with no gradient updates.

name: Neural scaling laws
summary: Loss falls as a power law in model size, data and compute.

name: Compute-optimal training
summary: For a fixed budget, grow parameters and training tokens together; most big LMs were undertrained.

name: Emergent abilities
summary: Abilities that are absent in small models and appear abruptly at scale.

name: Knowledge stored in LM parameters
summary: Answer factual questions from model weights alone, with no retrieval.

name: Prompt mining & paraphrasing
summary: Search for better prompts to get a truer read on what an LM knows.

name: Open-weights LLMs
summary: Release large LM weights so researchers can study and build on them.

name: Code LLMs & pass@k
summary: LMs fine-tuned on code, measured by whether sampled programs pass unit tests.

name: Trained verifiers
summary: Sample many solutions and let a trained verifier pick the right one.

name: Knowledge-grounded dialogue LMs
summary: Fine-tune dialogue models to consult external tools and knowledge for factual answers.

name: Instruction tuning
summary: Fine-tune on many tasks phrased as instructions, so the model follows new instructions zero-shot.

name: Crowdsourced instruction datasets
summary: Collections of tasks paired with human-written instructions, used to train and test instruction following.

name: Prompted multitask training
summary: Train on many datasets rewritten into diverse natural-language prompts.

name: Chain-of-thought in instruction tuning
summary: Include step-by-step reasoning examples in instruction tuning to unlock reasoning.

name: Proximal policy optimisation
summary: A simple, stable policy-gradient method with a clipped surrogate objective.

name: RL from human feedback
summary: Learn a reward model from human comparisons, then optimise the LM against it.

name: SFT → reward model → PPO pipeline
summary: Supervised demonstrations, then a preference reward model, then RL: the recipe behind chat assistants.

name: Recursive task decomposition
summary: Break a hard-to-judge task into smaller ones that humans can supervise.

name: Adapter modules
summary: Insert small trainable layers into a frozen network, one set per task.

name: Prefix tuning
summary: Optimise a few continuous 'virtual tokens' prepended at every layer of a frozen LM.

name: Soft prompt tuning
summary: Learn only input-level prompt embeddings; it rivals full fine-tuning at scale.

name: Frozen language model
summary: Keep a pretrained LM fixed and teach only a small module to feed it new information.

name: Instance discrimination
summary: Treat every image as its own class and learn features that tell instances apart.

name: Contrastive predictive coding / InfoNCE
summary: Predict future latents and score them against negatives with a contrastive loss.

name: Mutual-information maximisation
summary: Learn features by maximising information shared between an input and its encoding, or between views.

name: Momentum contrast
summary: A queue of negatives encoded by a slowly-updated momentum encoder.

name: Augmentations + projection head
summary: Strong augmentation plus a nonlinear projection head is what makes contrastive learning work.

name: Self-distillation without negatives
summary: An online network predicts a slowly-moving target network's view, with no negatives needed.

name: Masked image modelling
summary: Hide image patches and predict them, the vision analogue of BERT.

name: Masked autoencoders
summary: Mask 75% of patches, encode only the visible ones, and reconstruct pixels with a light decoder.

name: Semantic visual tokenizer (VQ-KD)
summary: Distil a semantic teacher into discrete codes, and use them as masked-prediction targets.

name: Masked prediction of CLIP features
summary: Reconstruct masked-out CLIP features, which scales a plain ViT to a billion parameters.

name: Off-the-shelf deep features
summary: Activations of an ImageNet CNN make strong generic features for new tasks.

name: Weakly supervised pre-training
summary: Use huge amounts of cheap, noisy labels instead of clean annotations.

name: Natural-language supervision for vision
summary: Train image models to predict free-form words and phrases from accompanying text.

name: Data scaling in vision
summary: Performance keeps rising (logarithmically) with 100× more labelled images.

name: Hashtag supervision at billion scale
summary: Pre-train on billions of social-media images labelled only by their hashtags.

name: Domain-adaptive pre-training data
summary: Reweight pre-training data towards the target domain; more data is not always better.

name: Teacher–student self-training
summary: A teacher labels a huge unlabelled pool; a student learns from those pseudo-labels.

name: Noisy Student training
summary: Self-training with an equal-or-larger student and noise added to it, iterated.

name: Big Transfer recipe
summary: Large-scale supervised pre-training plus a simple, fixed transfer heuristic.

name: Captioning as visual pre-training
summary: Learn visual backbones by generating captions, which is data-efficient compared to classification.

name: Joint image–text embedding
summary: Map images and sentences into one space so they can be retrieved by similarity.

name: Contrastive image–text learning
aliases: contrastive learning from paired images and text
summary: Pull matching image and text embeddings together and push mismatched pairs apart.

name: Zero-shot transfer via text prompts
summary: Classify into unseen classes by comparing an image with text descriptions of them.

name: Scaling on raw alt-text
summary: Skip expensive cleaning: a billion noisy alt-text pairs beat curated datasets.

name: Locked image tuning
summary: Keep a pretrained image tower frozen and train only the text side contrastively.

name: Vision foundation model
summary: One large image–text model adapted to classification, retrieval, detection, video and more.

name: Unified image–text–label contrastive
summary: Treat class labels and captions alike in one contrastive space.

name: Contrastive + captioning in one model
summary: One image–text encoder–decoder trained with both a contrastive and a captioning loss.

name: Object-detector region features
summary: Represent an image by features of detected object regions instead of a pixel grid.

name: Two-stream co-attention
summary: Separate image and text streams exchange information through co-attention layers.

name: Masked region modelling
summary: Mask image regions and predict their object class or features from the text and other regions.

name: Single-stream VL Transformer
summary: Concatenate words and image regions and run one Transformer over both.

name: QA as a pre-training task
summary: Add image question answering to the vision-language pre-training mix.

name: Shared encoder–decoder VLP
summary: One Transformer for both VL understanding and generation, switched by attention masks.

name: Word–region alignment
summary: Explicitly align words to image regions with an optimal-transport objective.

name: Adversarial training in embedding space
summary: Perturb word or region embeddings adversarially during training to generalise better.

name: Object tags as alignment anchors
summary: Feed detected object labels as text so they anchor image–text alignment.

name: VL-specific object detector
summary: A bigger detector trained on merged datasets gives much better region features for VL.

name: Multi-task vision-language learning
summary: Train one VL model on many tasks at once and share the representation.

name: Grid features instead of regions
summary: Plain convolutional grid features match region features for VQA and run 10× faster.

name: Detector-free patch VL Transformer
summary: Feed raw image patches straight into the VL Transformer: no CNN, no detector.

name: Align before fuse
summary: Align unimodal embeddings contrastively before fusing them with cross-attention.

name: Momentum distillation
summary: Learn from soft targets produced by a moving-average model, tolerating noisy web pairs.

name: Image–text matching (ITM)
summary: A binary classifier decides whether an image and a caption match, trained with hard negatives.

name: PrefixLM vision-language pre-training
summary: One generative prefix-LM objective on weakly aligned pairs replaces many task-specific losses.

name: Mixture of modality experts
summary: Shared attention with per-modality feed-forward experts, usable as a dual or fusion encoder.

name: Masked vision-language modelling
summary: Masked prediction over image patches and text tokens together, in one shared backbone.

name: Multiway Transformer (image as a foreign language)
summary: Treat images as another language and pre-train one multiway model with masked 'language' modelling on all.

name: Caption bootstrapping (CapFilt)
summary: Generate synthetic captions for web images and filter noisy ones, then retrain on cleaner data.

name: Multimodal mixture of encoder–decoder
summary: One model that acts as a contrastive encoder, a matching encoder or a caption decoder.

name: All VL tasks as text generation
summary: Answer every vision-language task by generating its label as text.

name: Every task as question answering
summary: Cast ten NLP tasks as QA over a context so one model handles them all.

name: Visual prefix for a frozen LM
summary: Turn an image into a few embeddings that a frozen LM reads as if they were words.

name: Perceiver resampler
summary: Learned queries cross-attend to many visual features and compress them to a fixed number of tokens.

name: Gated cross-attention layers
summary: New cross-attention layers inside a frozen LLM, gated to start as identity.

name: Interleaved image–text sequences
summary: Train and prompt on web pages where images and text alternate, enabling multimodal few-shot learning.

name: Querying Transformer (Q-Former)
summary: A lightweight Transformer whose learned queries extract the most text-relevant features from a frozen image encoder.

name: Two-stage vision-to-language bootstrapping
summary: First align the bridge with vision and text, then teach it to talk to a frozen LLM.

name: Visual word detectors for captioning
summary: Detect caption words with multiple-instance learning, then compose sentences with an LM.

name: Region–word visual-semantic alignment
summary: Align image regions with sentence fragments, then generate descriptions with a multimodal RNN.

name: Consensus caption metric (CIDEr)
summary: Score a caption by its TF-IDF n-gram agreement with many human references.

name: Novel object captioning
summary: Describe objects never seen in the caption training data.

name: Constrained beam search
summary: Force chosen tag words into generated captions at test time, without retraining.

name: Template-and-slot grounded captioning
summary: Generate a sentence template whose slots are filled by detected objects.

name: Object-relation graphs for captioning
summary: Encode semantic and spatial relations between objects with graph convolutions.

name: Meshed-memory captioning Transformer
summary: Memory-augmented region encoding plus mesh connectivity across encoder layers.

name: Bilinear (X-Linear) attention
summary: Second-order bilinear interactions inside attention for captioning.

name: Semantic concept tokens for captioning
summary: Detector-free captioning that predicts semantic concepts from ViT grid features.

name: Image-grounded text generation
summary: Train the model to generate the caption conditioned on the image.

name: Open-ended visual question answering
summary: Answer free-form natural-language questions about an image.

name: Symbolic reasoning for visual QA
summary: Answer questions by reasoning over uncertain scene parses in a probabilistic framework.

name: End-to-end neural VQA (CNN + LSTM)
summary: Encode the image with a CNN and the question with an LSTM, and train everything jointly.

name: Generating QA pairs from captions
summary: Turn existing image descriptions into question–answer training data automatically.

name: Balanced VQA against language priors
summary: Pair every question with images that flip the answer, so models must actually look.

name: Bilinear attention networks
summary: Attend over all question-word × image-region pairs with low-rank bilinear pooling.

name: Grounded visual reasoning
summary: Decide whether a statement is true of a pair of photos, which requires compositional reasoning.

name: Integrated ConvNet localisation & detection
summary: One shared ConvNet does classification, localisation and detection with dense sliding windows.

name: Region proposal network
summary: Predict object proposals from shared conv features, making two-stage detection near real-time.

name: Phrase grounding
summary: Link each phrase in a caption to the image region it mentions.

name: Box attention for visual relationships
summary: Model subject–object pairs inside a standard detector to find relationships.

name: Decoupled box proposal & featurisation
summary: Separate where-boxes-are from what-features-to-extract so more label data can be used.

name: Attention-unified detection head
summary: Unify scale, spatial and task awareness in a detector head with three attentions.

name: Dense image–language annotation
summary: Human-written regions, attributes and relationships that ground language in images.

name: Web-scale image–text pairs
summary: Hundreds of millions of image–caption pairs scraped from the web.

name: CLIP-filtered open datasets
summary: Use CLIP similarity to filter web pairs into an open, model-ready dataset.

name: Diverse curated text corpora
summary: Mix many high-quality text sources to improve LM generalisation.

name: PReLU & He initialisation
summary: Learnable leaky ReLUs plus an initialisation that lets very deep rectifier nets train from scratch.

name: Batch normalisation
summary: Normalise activations per mini-batch to stabilise and speed up training.

name: Knowledge distillation
summary: Train a small student to match a large teacher's softened predictions.

name: Label smoothing
summary: Soften one-hot targets to regularise the classifier.

name: Large-batch training recipe
summary: Scale learning rate with batch size and warm up, so huge batches train like small ones.

name: Decoupled weight decay (AdamW)
summary: Apply weight decay separately from Adam's adaptive step, fixing its regularisation.

name: Pipeline parallelism
summary: Split layers across devices and stream micro-batches through them.

name: Tensor (intra-layer) model parallelism
summary: Split each layer's matrices across GPUs so one model can be far larger than one device.

name: Automatic sharding
summary: Annotate a few tensors and let the compiler shard the whole computation.

name: 3D parallelism
summary: Combine data, tensor and pipeline parallelism to train 500B-parameter models.

name: Pathways multi-pod training
summary: Train one dense model across thousands of chips in multiple TPU pods.

name: Sparse mixture-of-experts layers
summary: Route each token to a few of many expert feed-forward layers: huge capacity, constant compute.

name: Top-1 (switch) routing
summary: Send each token to a single expert, simplifying MoE and scaling to trillions of parameters.

name: Extractive reading comprehension
summary: Answer a question by selecting a span from a passage.

name: Retriever–reader open-domain QA
summary: Retrieve documents, then read them to extract an answer.

name: Broad multitask knowledge benchmarks
summary: Test models across dozens to hundreds of academic and reasoning tasks at once.

name: True few-shot evaluation
summary: Evaluate few-shot ability without a hidden validation set used for tuning.

name: Natural distribution-shift robustness
summary: Accuracy drops on new test sets drawn the same way; robustness to such shifts is rare.

name: Corruption robustness
summary: Measure accuracy under noise, blur, weather and other common corruptions.

name: Texture vs shape bias
summary: ImageNet CNNs recognise textures more than shapes, unlike humans.

name: ImageNet accuracy predicts transfer
summary: Better ImageNet models are, almost linearly, better feature extractors elsewhere.

name: Discrete visual tokens (VQ-VAE)
summary: Compress images into a vocabulary of discrete codes so Transformers can model them like text.

name: Autoregressive text-to-image Transformer
summary: Model text and image tokens as one stream and sample images from text.

name: ViT-based image tokenizer
summary: A ViT-based VQGAN gives better image tokens for autoregressive image modelling.
